breach_notification_if_a_security_incide: Breach notification: if a security incident results in unauthorized access to your personal data, we will notify affected users and, where legally required, the relevant supervisory authority, without undue delay and in any case within the timeframe required by applicable law (e.g., 72 hours under GDPR Art. 33 once we become aware of a reportable breach), describing what happened, the data involved, and the steps we are taking.
claude_api_us_the_backup_ai: (Claude API, US): the backup AI model, used when Gemini fails, times out or is paused. Receives the same things as Google above. When a question depends on a real-world fact the sources cannot settle (for example whether a product is kosher), the AI may also ask Anthropic's web search to look it up on a short list of Orthodox sites, such as Chabad.org, the OU and Sefaria. That lookup sends only a short search phrase the AI wrote, never your name, email or history, and you can turn it off under Web search in the chat menu.

several_of_our_sub_processors_process: Several of our sub-processors process data in the United States. If you are located in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland, your data may be transferred to and processed in the US or other countries outside your jurisdiction. As confirmed 2026-09-04 from each provider's own public DPF/DPA documentation: Clerk and Vercel are self-certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (DPF), including its UK and Swiss extensions, with Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) incorporated as a fallback where DPF does not apply; Google participates in the DPF and additionally relies on SCCs for transfers outside DPF's coverage; Anthropic documents SCCs (EU Module 2/3, plus UK and Swiss transfer addenda) as its primary transfer mechanism and separately participates in the DPF as a secondary basis. As confirmed 2026-09-05 from their own current public documentation, Supabase relies solely on SCCs (Module 2/3, plus UK and Swiss transfer addenda), with no DPF self-certification found in its DPA; Sentry is self-certified under the EU-U.S. DPF, with SCCs (Module 2/3, plus a UK addendum) incorporated as a fallback where DPF does not apply. See docs/PRIVACY_OPERATIONS.md §3 for source links. These are the standard transfer safeguards recognized by the European Commission (Standard Contractual Clauses and, where applicable, the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework) and most services that rely on US-based providers use them for this purpose. Sh'elah relies on each vendor's own executed safeguard as confirmed above, and will review this section if a vendor's certification or DPA terms materially change.
shelah_is_currently_operated_by_akiva: Sh'elah is currently operated by Akiva Yevdayev, an individual, not a registered company, and has not formally designated an EU representative under GDPR Art. 27 or a Data Protection Officer under Art. 37. Sh'elah does not specifically market or target the Service to residents of the EU, UK, or Switzerland (no EU-specific advertising, currency, or localized marketing), does not carry out large-scale or systematic monitoring of users, and does not process special-category data as a core business activity. Any sensitive subject matter arises incidentally within a user's own question, not through systematic collection or profiling. Based on GDPR Article 27(2)'s exemption for occasional, low-risk, non-large-scale processing and Article 37's large-scale/systematic-monitoring threshold for a Data Protection Officer, Sh'elah has determined that neither an EU representative nor a DPO is currently required. This determination will be revisited if the Service's scale, EU-specific marketing, or data-processing activities materially change. Direct any EU-specific inquiry to the contact in §12.

the_service_is_not_directed_to: The Service is not directed to, and may not be used by, anyone under 13 years old (or under 16 in the EU/UK, absent verifiable parental consent; see our Terms of Service §3). We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone below these thresholds. If we learn that we have collected personal information from a user below the applicable threshold, we will delete that account and its data. If you believe a minor has provided us with personal information in violation of this policy, please contact us so we can investigate and delete it.

we_automatically_collect_certain_technic: We automatically collect certain technical information when you use the Service:
we_collect_information_about_how_you: We collect information about how you use the Service:
we_do_not_sell_or_share: We do not sell or share (as defined by CCPA/CPRA) your personal data to third parties for cross-context behavioral advertising.
we_do_not_sell_or_share_2: We do not sell or share personal data as those terms are defined by CCPA/CPRA, so there is nothing to opt out of today; we honor the Global Privacy Control (GPC) browser signal as a valid opt-out request for any future data sale/sharing regardless. You can also disable non-essential analytics cookies and unsubscribe from service emails.

we_may_update_this_privacy_policy: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will post the revised policy here with an updated effective date and version, and the footer notice on every page always links to the current version. For material changes (e.g., a new category of data collected, a new sub-processor with a materially different purpose, or a reduced level of protection), we will call out the change in the footer notice and, where practical, notify signed-in users directly, consistent with how we handle material changes to our Terms of Service (§18).
we_share_data_with_the_following: We share data with the following service providers ('sub-processors') who help us operate the Service, each under its own data-processing terms:
we_store_your_user_preferences_to: We store your user preferences to personalize your experience, including: language (English/Hebrew), theme (light/dark), community/tradition settings, and calendar display preferences.

we_use_cookies_and_similar_technologies: We use cookies and similar technologies:

we_will_not_deny_you_the: We will not deny you the Service, charge you a different price, or provide a different level of service because you exercised any of these rights
when_you_ask_a_question_without: when you ask a question without signing in, we set one cookie, shelah_device (a random value, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, one year), so the private link to your answer opens again in this browser. We store only a one-way hash of it next to that answer. It holds no profile, is not used for tracking or advertising, and is sent only to this site. Clear your cookies, or delete the answer from its page, to cut the link.
when_you_create_an_account_we: When you create an account, we collect your name and email address via our authentication provider (Clerk). We do not store your password directly. Clerk manages it securely.
where_processing_is_based_on_consent: Where processing is based on consent (e.g., any future non-essential cookies), withdraw it at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing before withdrawal
your_privacy_matters_shelah_does_not: Your Privacy Matters: Sh'elah does not sell your personal data. We collect only what we need to provide the Service and improve it. You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your data at any time.
your_question_the_earlier_turns_of: Your question, the earlier turns of the same conversation and the source excerpts found for it are sent to Google Gemini, or to Anthropic Claude if Gemini is unavailable, to write the answer. If you are signed in and short summaries of your earlier questions are stored for your account, up to two of them are sent too. This is automated, but it does not produce a legal or similarly significant decision about you. It writes study material, and the answer tells you to ask your own rabbi. See our AI Disclosure page for how this works and where it goes wrong.
